“All right, see you tomorrow! And don’t be late this time!”

Her words slightly slurred, she waves goodbye to her friends.

No one else is in sight. The taxi stand has fallen completely still.

Perhaps the car carrying her friends was the last one. Perhaps all the others are simply occupied.

The plaza before the station, so recently alive with crowds and flooded with light, has returned to a bloodless imitation of a place.

Assassin.

The figure cackles, and there can be no mistaking it for anyone but Zouken Matou.

He assaulted a woman and made her body his own in a matter of minutes.

However accomplished a mage may be, such speed is monstrous.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The laughing figure is indeed Matou Zouken.
It took him a few minutes to attack and take over a woman’s body.
The speed is incredible, even for a master magus.

pages.en:
“…I see. The woman’s original body was irrelevant. You merely required the flesh of a single human, which you then molded into the form you desired.

“In any event, worms fill the interior. They perform every function required of a human body. …Mimicry in its purest form.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I see. So you did not care who it was. All you require is a full body, no matter whose it may be. You merely mold the body to the shape you want.
What’s inside your body are worms in any case. The worms will function as your organs… It is indeed a mimicry.”

pages.jaRuby: 「ほほう。わずか一日で饒舌になったではないかアサシン。その様では、己が望みを思い出したか？」
pages.en: “Ho. A single day has made you remarkably eloquent, Assassin. Does this mean you have remembered your desire?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Oh my. In only one day, you have grown quite talkative. Do you remember your wish now?”

「

”

So long as he possesses flesh to serve as a breeding bed, and so long as the vessel of his soul—his true body—is not destroyed, he will continue to live.

Yes, Matou Zouken is almost immortal.
He will live as long as there are bodies to infest and his soul remains alive.

He transformed himself into something inhuman, then taught that thing to imitate a man.

The magecraft had limits.

It is no different from a machine. Theoretically, a machine may operate forever, but the parts that embody the theory rust with passing years.

The parts corrode. The gears slip from alignment. The program called thought can no longer keep pace with an age that never ceases to change.

Turning his body into something inhuman and mimicking human form.

Parts rust. Cogwheels slide out of place. Programs become obsolete.

pages.en:
“Kakaka. Nothing of the sort. My worms are vigorous. The flesh itself presents no difficulty. I became a parasite precisely because I feared the aging of my body, and I spared no preparation in defending against physical decline.

“I chose this method of prolonging life because I believed it would allow me to live forever while remaining human.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Haha, that is not true. The worms are lively. They have no problem as a body. From the start, I became a parasite in grief over my aging body. They serve perfectly as a body.
I chose this method to prolong my life forever while retaining my humility.”

pages.en:
“…I understand less than before. You chose perfect preservation of the body, yet this is the result? And why imitate the appearance of an old man at all?

“If you knead flesh like clay, you should be capable of assuming any shape.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I am even more confused. Is that all you can manage, even with the power to perfectly preserve your body? First of all, why are you taking the form of an old man?
If you are able to shape the flesh into any form, you should be able to take any appearance.”

肉体を元の形に戻すものはなんだと思う？」

肉体は己の肉体を記録している。肌が削げ、肉が落ちようとかつての姿に戻るのは、肉体そのものに遺伝子があるからだ」

“An excellent question. Then answer one of mine. Imagine a creature whose original body has been completely lost, and which attempts to restore that former body through its own power.

“What do you suppose returns its flesh to the original form?”

“—The body preserves a record of itself. Skin may be flayed and flesh may fall away, yet it returns to its former shape because the body itself contains the blueprint called genes.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“That is a good question. Then let me ask you. Let’s say something that lost its original body tries to reproduce its body with its powers.
In that case
what do you think restores the body to its original form?”
“
The body records itself. Even after it is burned or cut, the body is able to restore its original appearance, because there is an internal blueprint.”

pages.ja:
「うむ。遺伝子に記録された構成図じゃな。だがワシの場合は違う。そも、自身の構成を記録していた遺伝子そのものを失ったのだ。肉体を以って肉体を復元する事はできぬ。
その場合
自己を覚え、元通りの“カタチ”にするモノはなんだと思うね？」
pages.jaRuby:

“Yes. A plan recorded in the genes. But my case is different. I lost the genes—the very flesh that recorded my composition. Flesh cannot serve as the means of restoring flesh.

“In that event, what remembers the self and returns it to its original ‘form’?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yes. A body’s composition is recorded in its genes. But it is different in my case. I lost my body, the place where my composition was recorded. I can no longer use that blueprint to recreate my body.
In that case
what do you think records my body and gives it form?”

pages.en:
“Naturally. I do not choose an old man’s body because it pleases me.

“…Listen well. This is the only shape I can create, and a defective shape it is, for it must be replaced at intervals or rot away. Once, a single replacement sustained me for more than fifty years. Now, I must change bodies every few months to remain alive.

“…Who could understand such wretchedness, such torment of decay? Do not mistake me, Assassin of this age. Never call such a state immortality again—”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Of course. I am not taking form as an old man because I want to.
…Look, this is the only form I can create. And it is a poor creation that rots away unless I exchange it periodically. I used to be able to last fifty years before I had to exchange my body, but I have to exchange it every few months now.
…Who can understand the pain I feel as I rot away? Do not misunderstand, Assassin of this generation. Do not call such a thing immortality
”

“…Now I understand. Then the thing rotting is not your flesh, but—”

“…Precisely. My soul is rotting.

“The accumulation of time leaves its mark even upon the spiritual body. That is why my body decays. If the soul that serves as its blueprint is rotten, what else could the flesh do but putrefy?”

“…I understand now. So what is rotting is not your body, but…”
“…Yes, my soul is rotting.
Time even affects ethereal bodies. Therefore, my physical body will rot. It is natural for my body to rot if my soul, the blueprint of my body, is rotten.”

“Hm. And thus you seek the Holy Grail.

“…No wonder you are enraged. To know eternity only imperfectly may be more painful than never knowing it at all.”

“Indeed.

“…My body rots. It rots. I must be delivered from that agony—from the poison called time, which seeps into the marrow of my bones…!

“That is why I seek the Holy Grail. That is why I seek a body which cannot die.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hm
so that is why you seek the Holy Grail.
…No wonder you are angry. Such eternity must be more painful to you than those who have no idea of eternity.”
“Exactly.
…My body rots. I need to be freed from this pain, from this poison violating deep into my bones…!
The Holy Grail exists for that purpose. I have persisted for that purpose.”

“…Yes. I do not wish to die. I want to exist a little longer. The mere thought of vanishing from this world fills me with terror…!

“To escape that fate, I have lived for centuries. To escape decay, I have devoured the flesh of thousands…! Do you understand, lord of the mountain? I loathe the thing I have become, this body of worms. I resent that I alone must rot. I hate the insects called humans, who receive proper bodies as though it were their natural right——!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Right. I do not want to die. I want to live. It is dreadful to think that I will disappear from this world…!
To escape this fate, I have lived for hundreds of years, devouring the flesh of thousands…! Do you understand, master of the mountain? I hate myself for turning myself into worms. I hate being the only one who rots away. I hate all humans for being given bodies as a matter of course
!”

“——”

The white mask looks silently down upon the old man as he festers.

…He speaks boldly of resenting those who live in peace.

The method he chose to escape that peace has merely become the source of his torment.

The mage brought this suffering upon himself: the “decay” that melts his skin, putrefies his flesh, and gnaws at his bones for every moment he remains alive.

pages.en:
No ordinary person could endure the pain and terror of their own body rotting for even an hour.

No strength of mind would be enough.

The victim would die.

After an hour of decay, the flesh itself would perish.

Yet he has endured it for two hundred years.

No one but the old mage could begin to understand how far the mind of a “human” must rot after enduring the decay of its own flesh without end.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The pain and fear of experiencing one’s own decomposition must be unbearable for normal human beings.
Nobody should be able to endure it, no matter how strong their mind may be.
Because one will die.
The body dies if it rots for over an hour.
But two hundred years!
Only this old magus would understand how rotten the mind is of someone who has his body rotting away.
